summary.title: The (Real) 11 Reasons I Don't Hire You
summary.one_liner: Charity Majors explains the eleven practical reasons early-stage startups decline candidates, most of which concern team needs, scarcity and fit rather than individual merit.
keywords: hiring for team needs not individuals
takeaways: Early-stage startups hire from very few slots tied to key goals, so rejection is often about scarcity and team needs rather than personal worth.
Teams hire for what they lack collectively (skills, level, management potential), not for an abstract ranking of individuals.
Communication skills are weighted heavily; the technical interview involves extending code and discussing it with peers the next day.
Candidates should check that their expectations (predictability, on-call, pace) match a startup's reality.
A rejection is seldom a rejection of the person; the author says they hold declined candidates in high regard.
summary.summary: This is a blog post by Charity Majors, CEO of Honeycomb, written for job candidates who were turned down. It lists eleven common reasons her company declines people, including scarcity of hiring slots, team composition needs, being too senior or too junior for the role, lack of matching work, communication skills, and mismatched expectations about startup life. The tone is candid and aimed at reducing the sting of rejection, ending with the point that the company is evaluating its own ability to support a new hire as much as the candidate.
